label: D1 after a reward, upcoming choice a1, first half of episode
explanation: Fires only at D1, almost always when the reward input is 1 (96% of mass), and only in the first ~50 trials of an episode (none after trial ~65). Within that, it fires when the agent is about to choose a1 (94% of mass is on a1 trials); the previous trial reaching S2 essentially never co-occurs with activation. Recorded predicate uses the upcoming action at D1, which is the agent own choice (legitimate to compute) but technically marked FUTURE; dev F1 0.85, mass recall 0.92. The closest predicate using only observed history, (phase == D1) & (in_rew == 1) & (prev_state != 2) & (ep_trial < 50), gets dev F1 0.78 (prec 0.69, mass recall 0.95), i.e. a rewarded-S1 signal (the window first trial has unknown prev_state). Never fires at GO or D2, on unrewarded D1s (except a few weak ones), or late in the episode. Magnitude: in top windows the largest activation is at the first rewarded a1/S1 D1 of a run and shrinks across consecutive rewarded repeats (1.0, 0.64, 0.58, 0.55); activations sit in a narrow mid-range of the value head (7.5-7.7).

issues: The factual claims hold. The feature is D1-only: 100% of activation mass is at D1, with 0 active steps at GO or D2. 96.3% of the mass has in_rew == 1. After ep_trial >= 65 there is only 0.005% of the mass, and at ep_trial >= 50 recall is just 0.041. 94.1% of the mass is on action == 1. D1 with prev_state == 2 has exactly 0 activations across 156k steps. The reported test scores reproduce (F1 0.844, mass recall 0.911).

Systematic false-positive class in the recorded predicate: D1 steps with in_rew == 1, action == 1, ep_trial < 50 and prev_state == 2 (the agent was rewarded at S2 and then switches to a1). That is 3228 dev steps with precision 0.000, about 39% of the predicate's 8285 dev false positives. The explanation itself says the feature never fires after S2, yet neither the predicate nor the label includes this.

Label overclaims and underspecifies. 'D1 after a reward, upcoming choice a1' should be 'after a reward obtained at S1 (or with no known previous state), with a1 upcoming'. Reward collected at S2 never drives the feature, even when a1 follows.
Adding prev_state != 2 to the original predicate raises dev F1 from 0.853 to 0.878 (precision 0.905) and test F1 from 0.844 to 0.870, with no loss of recall.

The future variable is not needed. Replacing action == 1 with the model's own D1 policy readout (choice > 0, which is observed and computed by the agent) gives dev F1 0.871 and test F1 0.860. That is far better than the explanation's observed-only alternative (dev F1 0.78) and close to the action-based predicate.

Remaining false positives are mostly later steps in long rewarded a1/S1 runs, where activation decays toward zero. This matches the claimed magnitude decay and is not an extra category. The remaining misses look scattered and low in magnitude (about 8-9% of the mass).
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after a reward at S1 (not S2), when the agent is about to choose a1 (rewarded-S1 stay signal), first ~50 trials of the episode
